deep.text: Rotaviruses are the most common cause of diarrhoeal disease among infants and young children.

deep.caption: Rotaviral enteritis is usually an easily managed disease of childhood, but among children under 5 years of age, rotavirus caused an estimated 151,714 deaths worldwide from diarrhoea in 2019.

deep.text: Nearly every child in the world is infected with a rotavirus at least once by the age of five.
The 11 species of rotaviruses are referred to as RVA, RVB, RVC, RVD, RVF, RVG, RVH, RVI, RVJ, RVK, and RVL.
The faeces of an infected person can contain more than 10 trillion infectious particles per gram; fewer than 100 of these are required to transmit infection to another person.
Rotaviruses are transmitted by the faecal–oral route, via contact with contaminated hands, surfaces and objects, and possibly by the respiratory route.
Rotaviruses are stable in the environment and have been found in estuary samples at levels up to 1–5 infectious particles per US gallon.
The viruses survive between 9 and 19 days.
Rotaviral enteritis is a mild to severe disease characterised by nausea, vomiting, watery diarrhoea, and low-grade fever.
The most common is RVA, and these rotaviruses cause more than 90% of rotavirus infections in humans.
